scope: All 184 units read (dhyāna, the 182½ verses of names): text for sense, translation and word glosses against the text. The text was not compared with the source page. The names are explained after Bhāskararāya’s commentary.

items.issue: medas is fat; “marrow-fat” blurred it with majjā (marrow) three verses later.
śukla, the seventh bodily constituent in this series, was veiled as “the vital essence”.
items.change: Now “abiding in the seed”, in line with the gloss.

items.issue: gomātā was “mother of the cow-tongued speech”, which is not a possible meaning.
items.change: Now “mother of cows, and of speech”.

items.issue: anityatṛptā was “ever content though never sated”; the name means content even with perishable offerings, as the gloss says.
The text has akāntā (with the a- marked), “who ends sin and sorrow”; the translation had kāntā, “the beloved”.
items.change: Corrected to agree with text and gloss.

items.issue: indragopa is the red velvet mite, not a firefly.

items.change: Now “possessed of well-being”, as in the translation.

items.issue: kḷipta is printed twice where the word is kḷpta: kadambamañjarīkḷiptakarṇapūra (verse 8) and līlākḷiptabrahmāṇḍamaṇḍalā (verse 128). It is a transliteration slip for the vowel ḷ; the word glosses have kḷpta.

As in the Viṣṇu Sahasranāma, for some names the translation and the word gloss give different traditional explanations: kalātmikā “whose Self is the digits of the moon” / “the soul of the arts”; guhāmbā “mother of Guha” / “who dwells in the cave of the heart”; bhagārādhyā “worshipped in the bhaga” / “in the orb of the sun”; kapardinī “wearer of the matted lock” / “consort of the Lord of matted hair”.
options: B. Make the word gloss repeat the translation.
C. Keep both and add one sentence to the page note saying that where they differ both are traditional.
items.recommend: C, the same choice as for the Viṣṇu Sahasranāma.
